nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِنَّا: the origin is «إننا»; the nūn was dropped for lightness. أَرْسَلْنا: the lām was made quiescent in origin because of the succession of vowels and because it is indeclinable (mabnī). نُوحاً: a foreign noun, declined because it has three letters. إِلى قَوْمِهِ: a collective noun; and it has been said: «قوم» is the plural of «قائم», like «تاجر» and «تجر». أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ: «أن» has the sense of explication; you say: "i.e., warn your people". It may also be in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "that he should warn your people" [Translator's note: so in the text, «بأن أنذر قومك»; i.e. "with [the message]: warn your people"]. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ: you put «قبل» in the genitive by "min" and inflected it because it is in construct with «أن».

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ: "an" here too may be in the sense of «أي» (that is), and it may be in the sense of "a warner [telling you] to worship Allah", its ṣila (relative clause) being «اعبدوا». وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ: conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ: jussive because it is the answer to the command. وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: conjoined to it. إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ إِذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ: the imperfect verb is not made jussive by "law" because it differs from the conditional particles in that it does not turn the past into the future.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t:
وَإِنِّي كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); and «ما» is joined to «كل» when it is in the sense of «إذا» (when). The answer is جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ فِي آذانِهِمْ: the singular is «إِصْبَع», feminine; one also says «أُصْبُع».
وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا: conjoined to it. Al-Farrāʾ said:
أَصَرُّوا: they persisted silently in disbelief.
وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا اسْتِكْباراً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of emphasis, and likewise ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهاراً; the implied form may also be "possessing openness".

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: إِسْراراً: also a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of emphasis.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ: that is, ask Him for forgiveness. إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً: that is, covering over the punishments of sins for whoever repents.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ: the answer to the command. مِدْراراً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السماء». The pattern mifʿāl is used for the feminine without hāʾ because it runs parallel to the verb; one says «امرأةٌ مِذكارٌ» (a woman who bears males) and «مِئناثٌ» (who bears females) without hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: It is reported that this was said to them because they had an intense love of wealth.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
Most of the exegetes hold that «الأطوار» (stages) means His creating you a drop of fluid, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh. And it has been said:
the diversity of appearances, because you see the creatures and distinguish between them in forms and speech; there must be a difference even if they resemble one another. That indicates a Disposer and Maker.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
طِباقاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «سبع». Al-Farrāʾ permitted
the genitive outside the Qur'an.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً: Abū Jaʿfar said: the most eminent thing reported about it is the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr:
the face of the moon is towards the heavens, so it is truly in them. وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجاً: two objects ...

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أنبت» is «إنبات»; however, the implied form is «فنبتّم نباتا» (and you grew a growing). It has been said: this is because Adam ﷺ was created from clay; and it has been said: the drop of fluid is created from dust.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيها: by burial. وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْراجاً: to the resurrection.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: [Bisāṭan] may also be [spelled] with a ṣād, because a ṭāʾ follows it.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: سُبُلًا فِجاجاً: he said: various roads.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
The Kufans and Abū ʿAmr read وَوَلَدُهُ [i.e. «وولدُه»] [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described];
«ووالدُه» [Translator's note: so in the text, «والده»; perhaps «وُلْده/أُلده» «وُلْدَه», with hamza for wāw, was intended, as the comparison with «أقّتت» suggests] is also permissible, like «أقّتت». Shibl reported from Mujāhid, who said: «وُلْدُه» is his wife and family. Khārija reported from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: «وُلْدُه» is his clan and people. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the lexicographers, apart from this report from Abū ʿAmr, they say: «ولد» and «وُلْد» are like «بَخَل» and «بُخْل», and «فَلَك» and "fulk"; and in their view «وُلْد» may be the plural of «ولد», [like] «وَثَن» and «وُثْن».

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
And «كُبَّاراً» [Translator's note: the variant reading referred to is not shown; presumably «كُبّارا», without doubling]:
it is a reading with the same meaning.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
وَقالُوا لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلا سُواعاً: this [i.e. «وُدّا», with ḍamma] is the reading of the people of Medina; the Kufans and Abū ʿAmr read وَدًّا with fatḥa on the wāw, which is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He argued from their saying «عبد وَدّ» and that the idol's name was «وَدّ». [Translator's note: the vowelled text shows «وَدًّا» in both places; the Medinan reading described is «وُدّا».] Abū Jaʿfar said: this is among the anomalous arguments; what is commonly known is the reverse of what he said: one says only «عبد وُدّ» [Translator's note: so in the text, the vowelling being implied]. If it is a matter of common usage, then it is this; and if it is a matter of what is most fitting, then the most fitting is that it should be named «وُدّ», derived from «الوداد», which is ease and softness. From it comes «وَدِدْتُ الرجلَ», I loved the man, and «وَدَدْتُه» when I treated him kindly; and «وَدِدْتُ أنّ ذلك الشيءَ لي», i.e. I wished with ease [that the thing were mine]; and their naming the idol «وُدّ» is from this. وَلا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْراً: «يغوث» and «يعوق» are not declined (lam yanṣarif) because they resemble the imperfect verb. Al-Aʿmash read «ولا يغوث ويعوق» declined [i.e. «يغوثا ويعوقا»]. In the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh, according to what is reported: وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلا سُواعاً وَلا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْراً [with tanwīn on «يغوث» and «يعوق»] [Translator's note: the vowelled text shows the standard reading]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, a solecism (laḥn), and it also contradicts the great body of the written text (al-sawād al-aʿẓam). Al-Farrāʾ claimed
that declining it is permissible because of its frequency, or as though it were indefinite. This does not hold, because it is not the case that when a thing is frequent, what is diptote in it becomes declined; besides, his saying
"because of its frequency" has no meaning for the name of an idol, and it has no meaning for something specific like this to be indefinite. Al-Kisāʾī went further than this and said: the Arabs decline every diptote except «أفعل منك» (more … than you). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is wrong, because they have declined «خيرا منك» and «شرا منك», with «منك» accompanying them.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً: outside the Qur'an, «وقد أضللنَ» and «وقد أضلّتْ» would be permissible. وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلالًا: it has been said: the meaning is "do not grant them success"; and it has been said: except straying from the reward and the way to Paradise.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
«ما» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; according to the Basrans nothing else is permissible. The Kufans say:
a connective (ṣila), and then in some places they return to the truth, and this is one of them. Al-Farrāʾ claimed ]
that «ما» here adds meaning, because the meaning is "because of their sins they were drowned", and he argued that «ما» indicates the conditional (mujāzāh), and mentioned «حيثما تكنْ أكنْ» (wherever you are, I shall be), and mentioned «كيف» and «أين» — this is in his book «Maʿānī al-Qurʾān». His position in this would be good were it not for the confusion in it: he mentioned «حيثما», with which the conditional is formed only when «ما» accompanies it; and he mentioned «كيف», with which the conditional is not formed at all; and he mentioned «أين», with which the conditional is formed both with «ما» and without «ما». So he combined three different things.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: That is, anyone; it is from «دار يدور», i.e. anyone who moves about. And it has been said: «ديّار» is the occupant of a dwelling (dār).

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلاَّ فاجِراً كَفَّاراً (27). إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ: a condition. يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ: the apodosis (mujāzāh). وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فاجِراً كَفَّاراً: conjoined to it.
